messages:
Sam: FYI we have NebulaOps POC kickoff tomorrow. They're asking about onboarding a custom sparse-adapter model and want a quick compatibility pass. Anyone can lead the model vet?
Ravi: I can take it. What's the model artifact name + perf targets?
Sam: Model: nebula-13b-extended-sparse.tar.gz. It's a 13B base with 40% structured sparsity plus an injected adapter for domain intents. They want 4k context support. Target p95 <450ms, initial qps 3, scale to ~15 for demo.
Lina: Sparse + adapters often change attention layout. We need their model config and the adapter merge script. Ask for the unmerged and merged versions so we can run diff checks.
Ravi: Agreed. First pass I run our validator. Tell them to run this locally and upload the report: 
```bash
python infra/tools/model_validate.py \ 
  --model nebula-13b-extended-sparse.tar.gz \ 
  --checks sparsity,adapter,attention,tokenizer \ 
  --out nebula_report.json
```
Quinn: Also need tokenizer files and vocab. For 4k contexts we check tokenizer max_length and surrogate tokens. If they used a custom BPE variant it'll change chunking.
Marta: Security note: we require SBOM + artifact provenance for any uploaded packages. For POC we allow a scanned VM image in our sandbox OR a presigned S3 link to the tar. Please provide an SBOM or a layered manifest.
sec-bot: Created ticket SEC-3300 for NebulaOps artifact review  https://jira.redwood/SEC-3300
ops-bot: Created ticket SALES-1133 NebulaOps POC onboarding  https://jira.redwood/SALES-1133 (assigned Ravi, Lina)
Ravi: Timeline: if they drop artifacts now I can run validator + attention-layout static check in ~1h. Sparse kernel compatibility test (to ensure we use our fused sparse matmul) takes another 1.5h on dev A40.
Lina: I'll run tokenizer and adapter merge sanity in parallel  ~30m. If adapter requires runtime hooks we may need a small shim.
Sam: Their infra asked about KV cache strategy for 4k context and whether Redwood supports segmented summaries. They specifically want to preserve the last 2k tokens verbatim and summarize older segments.
Quinn: We support hybrid: keep last N tokens as pinned segments + summarize older chunks. Config we typically provide:
```json
{
  "kv": {
    "mode": "hybrid",
    "pinned_tail_tokens": 2048,
    "summary_chunk_tokens": 1024,
    "evict_policy": "tombstone_compress",
    "summary_strategy": "semantic_rollup"
  }
}
```
Ravi: Note: pinned tail increases memory linearly. For demo scale (qps 15) recommend 2x A100 reserved to avoid tail latency spikes. I'll include perf extrapolations in the report.
Marta: Pricing: prepare two estimates. Hosted POC (metered) with a 20% test discount, and Dedicated trial pricing (hourly reserved + data-transfer). Add a small integration uplift for adapter support (~10%).
Sam: POC length = 10 business days. No SLA requested for POC. They did ask about long term Dedicated SLA options.
Lina: If their adapter requires custom ops we'll need a verified variant in the catalog with a build-id and a fallback to a slower kernel. We'll mark such variants: [adapter-custom, sparse-verified].
Ravi: If validator shows unsupported ops I'll open a runtime-infra ticket. Otherwise plan: create temporary catalog entry nebula-13b-sparse-adapter:dev + run microbench.
Quinn: For microbench use this script (we'll capture p50/p95 and token/s):
```bash
python infra/tools/microbench.py --model /tmp/nebula \ 
  --context 4096 --batch 1 --tokens 1024 --quant dynamic
```
Sam: Great. I'll ask them to upload artifacts to SALES-1133 and sign the temporary NDA for sandbox uploads. Also ask for an MD5 + source manifest.
sec-bot: Note from security: require ephemeral credentials for upload and artifact auto-delete after 7 days in sandbox.
Marta: I'll draft pricing lines and attach to SALES-1133, plus call out expected cost delta for pinned tail memory.
Sam: Thanks team. I'll ping when artifacts are in. Quinn/Ravi/Lina, pls ack once you start tests. :rocket:
